narration: The pipeline starts with the input image. A frozen CLIP visual encoder turns it into the visual feature map F_v.
In parallel, class prompts such as 'A photo of a person, bicycle, road' go through the CLIP language encoder to give the text embedding F_t.
Vision-language correlation compares F_v with F_t, producing the correlation volume C of vision-and-language similarity maps.
Everything inside the purple panel is one ESC-Block, and the block is stacked and repeated N times.
Inside the block, the SAM Block refines the visual features, yielding the enhanced feature map F_v prime.
The correlation volume is also fed to PPG, the pseudo prompt generator.
PPG emits pseudo prompts: candidate point locations and coarse mask proposals for the target classes.
The VLF Block fuses the refined visual features, the pseudo prompts and the text features, updating the correlation volume to C prime.
After N iterations, the decoder maps the refined correlations to the final predicted segmentation mask M.
